text:
aisha: quick sync — proposing we standardize on progressive verification for safetensors shards when doing streaming decryption during hotpatches. rationale: reduce tail latency and avoid blocking whole-model validation.

ben: curious — progressive verify = verify layer header + checksum as chunk arrives, then decrypt/commit bytes for that chunk?

carlos: yeah, basically chunk-level integrity first, then background full-blob verification. that way inference can start earlier for unaffected layers.

dana: two immediate risk buckets: 1) partial-corruption that only shows up during final verify, 2) replay/consistency when switching shards mid-flight. need guardrails.

ben: suggestion: attach a short manifest with per-chunk checksums + version nonce. streaming consumer accepts chunk if chunk-checksum matches and manifest nonce ties to checkpoint id. final verification replays manifest and marks checkpoint as fully-valid.

aisha: +1. also propose we maintain a "staged" SPIKE state: model can be served from staged shards but flagged; traffic routed with canary traffic weighting and builtin fallback to prior model if a final-verify fails.

loader-bot: [deploy] hotpatch 2026-03-21T15:02:03Z - staged model v=rlw-2026-03-21-07 accepted (progressive_verify enabled).

carlos: implementation note: our current streaming pipeline assumes atomic shard commit. we need small refactor: allow per-chunk commit into ephemeral kvcache, with commit log entry per chunk. existing eviction logic needs to be aware (evict should only remove chunks not referenced by active checkpoint ids).

ben: perf tradeoff: more metadata updates -> more IOPS. mitigate by batching commit-log writes every N chunks or on layer boundary. and we can rely on kvcache GC to trim old checkpoint ids asynchronously.

dana: about replay/consistency — if we get half-updated manifest and then a reconnect supplies different ordering, we must ensure idempotence. plan: manifest includes checkpoint id + sequence numbers per chunk; loader rejects nonmonotonic sequences unless a tombstone-reset occurs.

aisha: question: do we prefer streaming-decrypt-then-verify or verify-then-decrypt for each chunk? verify-first adds extra read if encryption layer is separate. decrypt-first allows checksum on plaintext which is what safetensors does currently.

carlos: leaning decrypt-first for performance if decryption is cheap (AES-GCM in hardware). verify-on-plaintext avoids checksum-on-ciphertext mismatch problems across transports. but we need constant-time failure semantics to avoid leaking side-channels.

ben: crypto note: with AES-GCM we get authenticity from AEAD — if we trust transport + AEAD, maybe chunk-level AEAD tag can replace a separate checksum. but not all backends preserve AEAD tags in our blobstore; some store cipherstream without metadata.

dana: operationally we should support three modes: conservative (full-blob verify before serve), progressive (serve on chunk-verify + staged commit), and permissive (serve immediately with best-effort background verify). customers can opt by SLA tier.

aisha: decision proposal: default to progressive mode with these constraints: 1) manifest required with chunk checksums and checkpoint id, 2) ephemeral staged state for chunks until final verify marks checkpoint stable, 3) canary traffic + automatic fallback, 4) delayed eviction that keeps checkpoint id references for 2x safe window.

carlos: agree. follow-ups: API change for weights-source to return chunk-level metadata + checkpoint id. loader refactor to support chunk-commit API. telemetry to add metrics: chunk_accept_rate, final_verify_fail_rate, staged_rollback_count.

ben: I'll own the loader refactor (PR draft by Fri). Carlos will own the weights-source manifest addition. Dana — add rollback playbook and SLO changes. Aisha — validate canary rollout thresholds.

dana: flagged: need to update Console to show "staged" models and a rollback button. otherwise oncall will panic. :point_up:

loader-bot: [telemetry] staged_accept=37 staged_reject=2 final_verify_fail=0 (last 12h).

aisha: thanks all. if no objections by EOD I'll post a quick RFC follow-up summarizing decision + tasks.

ben: no objections from me.

carlos: SGTM.

dana: SGTM.
